climate.overview_html: August 27’s twin headline: global ocean temperatures hit their all-time daily record on August 22 — Copernicus C3S confirms the daily global mean SST reached 21.1°C, breaking the previous record set in March 2024 and unusually occurring in August, a month when SSTs historically cool, driven by the developing super El Niño and long-run anthropogenic warming. Simultaneously, Indonesia’s wildfire emergency has escalated dramatically: 285,000 hectares have burned and 3.4 million people are at respiratory risk, with cross-border haze now threatening Malaysia’s National Day celebrations on August 31 and 600 schools closed in Sarawak. The eastern China coast faces a compounding hazard: Typhoon Narra made landfall in Hainan then Guangdong on August 25–26, saturating soils hours before Typhoon Saudel bears down on Zhejiang and Fujian.

items.headline: Global Ocean SST Sets All-Time Daily Record: 21.1°C on August 22 — Breaks March 2024 Peak; Unprecedented Because August Is Climatologically a Cooling Month
items.summary: Copernicus C3S data confirm the global-average daily sea surface temperature reached 21.1°C on August 22, 2026, breaking the previous all-time daily record set in March 2024. The timing is climatologically remarkable: August is historically a month of gradual SST cooling as the Northern Hemisphere summer peak passes, making a new global maximum doubly unusual. Scientists attribute the record to the convergence of the intensifying super El Niño (NOAA CPC >90% probability of ONI exceeding +2.0°C) and the long-run anthropogenic ocean warming trend. Scientific American notes the milestone places 2026 on a trajectory well above 2023’s record-shattering ocean-temperature year. Elevated SSTs amplify tropical cyclone intensification, marine heatwave extent and intensity, and atmospheric moisture available for extreme precipitation.

items.headline: Indonesia Fires Scale to 285,000 ha; 3.4M at Respiratory Risk; Haze Threatens Malaysia’s National Day (Aug 31); 600 Sarawak Schools Closed; Malaysia Grants Cross-Border Cloud-Seeding Airspace
items.summary: Indonesia’s El Niño-driven wildfire and haze emergency has escalated sharply since August 25. Total area burned has reached approximately 285,000 hectares, with the national disaster agency (BNPB) reporting 3.4 million people at risk from respiratory illness across Sumatra and Kalimantan. Dense transboundary smoke is affecting peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak; Malaysian officials are weighing whether to cancel or curtail National Day celebrations on August 31, with 600 schools in Sarawak already closed. As a reciprocal emergency measure, Malaysia granted Indonesian cloud-seeding aircraft permission to operate in Malaysian airspace over Sarawak. Indonesia’s BMKG warned additional hot dry conditions are expected through at least early September under strong El Niño forcing.

items.headline: Back-to-Back Typhoons Strike Eastern China: Narra Makes Landfall in Hainan Then Guangdong (Aug 25–26); Waterlogged Soils Compound Saudel Flood Risk on Zhejiang/Fujian Coast
items.summary: Typhoon Narra made successive landfalls in Hainan Province and Guangdong on August 25–26 before weakening to a tropical depression. China’s CMA confirmed Narra deposited heavy rainfall across Guangdong, Fujian, and Zhejiang — provinces now in the projected path of Typhoon Saudel tracking toward landfall on the night of August 27 into August 28. With soils already saturated from Narra, hydrological models warn that Saudel’s rainfall will generate disproportionately high runoff and flash-flood potential. The back-to-back typhoon sequence is consistent with elevated Western Pacific activity expected under super El Niño conditions, where SST anomalies in the region are running 1.5–2.0°C above climatology.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel — Hours From Landfall on Zhejiang/Fujian Coast; 11,000 Vessels Sheltered in Fujian; Rail and Tourism Suspended in Eastern China; Back-to-Back With Narra on Saturated Soils
major_events.status: LANDFALL IMMINENT · ZHEJIANG/FUJIAN COAST · AUG 27–28 · FLOOD HAZARD PRIMARY
major_events.impact: Typhoon Saudel is hours away from landfall on China’s Zhejiang/Fujian coast on the night of August 27 into August 28, having moved through the East China Sea after clearing Okinawa (Category 1 equivalent at ~90 mph) on August 26. Bloomberg confirms heavy rain is already affecting saturated southeastern China as the storm approaches. Chinese authorities sheltered more than 11,000 fishing and cargo vessels in Fujian ports; Zhejiang suspended high-speed rail service and closed tourist sites. The core hazard is flooding, not wind: soils across the eastern China coastal corridor are already saturated from Typhoon Narra (Hainan/Guangdong landfall Aug 25–26), and Saudel’s rainfall is expected to generate extreme runoff and river flooding in densely populated lowlands.

major_events.name: US South/Southwest Heat Dome — Records Shattering Aug 27; Death Valley Near 126°F; Dallas 100°F+ on 27 of 31 August Days; 24M Under Extreme-to-Major Risk; Event May Extend Into September
major_events.status: ACTIVE · RECORDS SHATTERING · DEATH VALLEY 126°F · EXTENDING INTO SEPTEMBER
major_events.impact: The US South and Southwest heat dome continued to shatter temperature records on August 27. Death Valley was forecast to approach 126°F (52.2°C), and Dallas recorded its 27th day at or above 100°F in August alone. Approximately 12 million people remain under extreme heat risk and another 12 million under major heat risk across the Desert Southwest, southern Plains, and Texas. AccuWeather and Fox Weather forecasters warn the blocking pattern may extend into early September as El Niño-driven upper-level ridging maintains the dominant high. July 2026 averaged 76.89°F across the Lower 48 — the hottest US July in 131 years — and August is tracking to extend that record.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — FATALITY CONFIRMED: 80-Year-Old Woman Dies Fleeing Meadow Valley; ~12,000 Under Evacuation Orders; BC Provincial State of Emergency Declared
major_events.status: FATAL · OUT OF CONTROL · ~12,000 EVACUATED · BC STATE OF EMERGENCY
major_events.impact: An 80-year-old woman died while fleeing the Bald Range wildfire near Meadow Valley, BC, becoming the first confirmed wildfire fatality of the 2026 BC season. Approximately 12,000 residents remain under evacuation orders across Summerland, Peachland, and surrounding communities. BC Premier David Eby declared a provincial state of emergency for the Southern Interior. The fire, discovered August 7, grew beyond 25,000 ha by August 25; BC Wildfire Service warns high temperatures and low humidity will sustain extreme fire behavior through the weekend. Smoke continues to generate air-quality alerts across northern Washington, Idaho, and Montana.

major_events.name: Indonesia Wildfire/Haze Emergency — 285,000 ha Burned; 3.4M at Respiratory Risk; Haze Threatens Malaysia National Day (Aug 31); 600 Sarawak Schools Closed
major_events.status: ESCALATING · 285,000 HA · MALAYSIA CROSS-BORDER HAZE · 3.4M AT RISK
major_events.impact: Indonesia’s wildfire emergency has escalated from approximately 3,500 hotspots on August 25 to an estimated 285,000 hectares burned as of August 27. BNPB reports 3.4 million people at respiratory risk across Sumatra and Kalimantan as peatland fires produce dense, persistent haze. Transboundary smoke has reached peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak; Malaysian authorities closed 600 schools in Sarawak and are weighing cancellation of National Day celebrations on August 31. Malaysia granted Indonesia permission for cross-border cloud-seeding operations in Malaysian airspace. Strong El Niño conditions — ONI expected to exceed +2.0°C — are sustaining the prolonged dry season enabling rapid fire escalation.

major_events.name: Atlantic Basin — Invest 96L Under Monitoring; NHC at 70% Development Odds Aug 25 Before El Niño Shear Cut Probability to ~20–40%; Below-Normal Season Continues
major_events.status: INVEST 96L MONITORED · 20–40% ODDS · EL NIÑO SHEAR SUPPRESSION
major_events.impact: After several weeks of quiet, the Atlantic basin now has Invest 96L under NHC monitoring. The disturbance was assigned a 70% 5-day development probability on August 25 before El Niño-related wind shear over the Main Development Region cut that estimate to approximately 20–40% by August 26–27. NOAA’s below-normal Atlantic season outlook remains in effect. Forecasters note Invest 96L bears watching through the weekend but that the shear environment currently favors minimal organization. The Atlantic has produced zero named storms to date in August 2026.

major_events.name: Europe Fire/Drought Emergency — 505,683 ha Burned EU-Wide (33% Ahead of Record-2025 Pace); Danube Critically Low; Paks Nuclear Output Cut
major_events.status: ONGOING · 505,683 HA · VERY-EXTREME FIRE DANGER · DROUGHT ALERT LEVEL
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area has reached 505,683 hectares — 33% ahead of the same period in 2025, itself a record year at 1,034,552 ha total. Very-extreme fire danger persists across the Romania–Hungary corridor, with extreme danger reaching southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. JRC’s Copernicus European Drought Observatory documents warning-to-alert-level drought across 50% of EU+UK territory, with the Danube running critically low and Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant reducing output due to inadequate cooling-water temperatures.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — Toll ≥126 Since June 26; Heavy-Rain Pulses Ongoing
major_events.status: ONGOING · FLASH FLOODING · PUNJAB / KP / SINDH
major_events.impact: Pakistan’s cumulative monsoon death toll since June 26 stands at or above 126 per PDMA, with successive fresh heavy-rain pulses producing flash flooding across northern and central Pakistan. PMD continues to flag further heavy-rain risk in coming days. The 2026 monsoon has produced repeated flash-flood pulses across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh — not on the 2022 catastrophic scale, but on pace to be one of the more damaging monsoons of the decade.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Saudel is hours from landfall on China’s Zhejiang/Fujian coast as of the August 27 digest — making landfall against soils already saturated by Typhoon Narra (Hainan/Guangdong, Aug 25–26), with 11,000 vessels sheltered in Fujian, high-speed rail suspended in Zhejiang, and tourist sites closed across the eastern coast. The Bald Range wildfire in BC has claimed its first fatality — an 80-year-old woman who died fleeing Meadow Valley — as approximately 12,000 remain under evacuation orders and BC declares a provincial state of emergency. Indonesia’s fires have grown to 285,000 ha with 3.4 million at respiratory risk, cross-border haze threatening Malaysia’s National Day on August 31 and forcing closure of 600 Sarawak schools. In the US, the heat dome continues to set records with Death Valley near 126°F and the event potentially extending into September. The Atlantic has broken its quiet streak with Invest 96L under NHC monitoring, though El Niño shear has cut development odds to 20–40%.

items.headline: Typhoon Saudel Brings Heavy Rain to Saturated Southeastern China: 11,000 Vessels Sheltered in Fujian; Rail Suspended in Zhejiang; Flood Hazard Primary as Narra-Soaked Soils Await Second Storm
items.summary: Bloomberg confirms Typhoon Saudel is bringing heavy rain to southeastern China on August 27 as the storm approaches its landfall on the Zhejiang/Fujian coast overnight into August 28. The primary concern is flooding, not wind: soils across the eastern China coastal corridor are already saturated from Typhoon Narra (Hainan/Guangdong, Aug 25–26), making Saudel’s rainfall far more hydrologically dangerous than its Category-1-equivalent winds would suggest. More than 11,000 fishing and cargo vessels sheltered in Fujian harbors; Zhejiang suspended high-speed rail service and closed provincial tourist sites. China issued its highest-level typhoon emergency response for coastal Zhejiang and Fujian, with hundreds of thousands of residents in low-lying areas under evacuation notices.

items.headline: BC Wildfire FATALITY: 80-Year-Old Woman Dies Fleeing Bald Range Fire Near Meadow Valley — First BC Wildfire Death of 2026; ~12,000 Under Evacuation Orders; Provincial State of Emergency Declared
items.summary: An 80-year-old woman died on August 27 while attempting to evacuate from Meadow Valley near Summerland, becoming the first confirmed fatality from British Columbia’s 2026 wildfire season. Approximately 12,000 residents remain under evacuation orders across Summerland, Peachland, and surrounding communities as the Bald Range fire continues to burn out of control. BC Premier David Eby declared a provincial state of emergency for the Southern Interior. The fire was discovered on August 7 and has grown beyond 25,000 hectares; extreme fire behavior is expected to continue with hot, dry, and gusty conditions forecast through the weekend. Smoke continues to produce air-quality alerts across northern Washington, Idaho, and Montana.

items.headline: Indonesia Haze Crisis Deepens: 285,000 ha Burned; 3.4M at Respiratory Risk; Cross-Border Smoke Threatens Malaysia’s National Day (Aug 31); 600 Sarawak Schools Closed
items.summary: Indonesia’s haze crisis accelerated sharply on August 27 as fires now cover an estimated 285,000 hectares, with 3.4 million people at respiratory risk from persistent peatland smoke across Sumatra and Kalimantan. Transboundary haze has entered peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak, with air quality degrading sharply across multiple Malaysian cities. Malaysian officials are weighing cancellation or curtailment of National Day celebrations on August 31; 600 schools in Sarawak are already closed. As an emergency response, Malaysia granted Indonesian weather aircraft permission to conduct cross-border cloud-seeding operations in Sarawak airspace. Indonesia’s BMKG warned that strong El Niño conditions will sustain below-average rainfall through at least early September.

items.headline: US Heat Dome Sets Records Aug 27: Death Valley Near 126°F; Dallas 100°F+ on 27 of 31 August Days; 24M Under Extreme-to-Major Risk; Pattern May Extend Into September
items.summary: The US South and Southwest heat dome continued to shatter temperature records on August 27. Death Valley was forecast to approach 126°F (52.2°C), and Dallas registered its 27th day at or above 100°F in August 2026 alone. Fox Weather reports approximately 12 million people under extreme heat risk and another 12 million under major heat risk across the Desert Southwest, southern Plains, and Texas. AccuWeather forecasters warned the blocking pattern shows no sign of collapse before month’s end and may persist into early September under El Niño-driven upper-level ridging. The heat event follows a July 2026 that averaged 76.89°F across the Lower 48, the hottest US July in 131 years of records.

items.headline: Atlantic Watch: Invest 96L at 70% Development Odds Aug 25 Before El Niño Shear Cut Probability to ~20–40%; Below-Normal Season Pattern Continues After Three Quiet Weeks
items.summary: After three weeks of quiet in the Atlantic Main Development Region, NHC placed Invest 96L at 70% 5-day development odds on August 25 — the first significant Atlantic tropical disturbance since Invest 97L failed to develop. El Niño-related wind shear over the Main Development Region cut those odds to approximately 20–40% by August 26–27, consistent with NOAA’s below-normal season outlook. Fox Weather meteorologists note Invest 96L bears watching through the weekend but that the current wind-shear environment strongly favors minimal organization. The Atlantic has produced zero named storms to date in August 2026.

renewables.overview_html: The structural milestone of the first half of 2026 is now official: US wind and solar reached 20% of total electricity generation in H1 2026, outpacing both coal and nuclear for the first time, with output up 10% year-on-year despite the expiration of some federal incentives; 8.3 GW of battery storage was added in the same six months. The period’s headline project: Pattern Energy’s SunZia Wind Project in New Mexico — 3,650 MW, 916 turbines, $11 billion — commissioned in June as the largest wind farm in the Western Hemisphere, with 550-mile HVDC transmission serving 3 million homes in Arizona and Southern California. On the storage-technology frontier, UK-based Certain Energy closed a €11.6 million Series A on August 26, backed by the British Business Bank, Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate, to scale its manganese-based flow battery chemistry for long-duration energy storage.

items.headline: Pattern Energy SunZia 3,650 MW Wind Project (New Mexico) Now Fully Commissioned — Largest Wind Farm in Western Hemisphere; 916 Turbines, $11B Cost, 550-Mile HVDC Transmission, Powers 3M Homes
items.summary: Pattern Energy’s SunZia Wind Project in Torrance and Lincoln counties, New Mexico, reached full commercial operation in June 2026, becoming the largest wind farm in the Western Hemisphere at 3,650 MW. The project deploys 916 wind turbines across 240,000 acres and is paired with the SunZia Southwest Transmission project, a 550-mile HVDC line delivering clean power to Arizona and Southern California markets and serving approximately 3 million homes. Total capital investment topped $11 billion, making SunZia the largest privately financed renewable energy project ever built in the US. EIA’s Today in Energy analysis notes SunZia’s commissioning marks a structural shift in the Southwest’s generation mix, displacing natural gas peaking capacity during summer demand peaks intensified by El Niño conditions.

items.headline: US Wind + Solar Hit 20% of Grid Generation in H1 2026 — Outpacing Coal and Nuclear for First Time; Output Up 10% Year-on-Year Despite Federal Headwinds; 8.3 GW Battery Added
items.summary: US wind and solar power output grew 10% in H1 2026 compared to H1 2025, reaching a combined 20% share of total US electricity generation — surpassing both coal and nuclear on a generation basis for the first time. The milestone came despite the expiration of key federal tax incentives and sustained political headwinds for clean energy policy. EIA data show 8.3 GW of utility-scale battery storage capacity was added in H1 2026, cementing battery storage as the primary firm-capacity complement to intermittent renewables. The structural shift is attributed to long-term contract commitments, falling capital costs, and state-level policy support that has offset federal policy uncertainty.

items.headline: Certain Energy Closes €11.6M Series A — British Business Bank Leads; Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, Temasek Catalytic Capital Back Imperial College London Spinout’s Manganese Flow Battery for LDES
items.summary: Certain Energy, a UK-based long-duration energy storage company spun out of Imperial College London, closed a €11.6 million Series A on August 26, 2026. The round was led by the British Business Bank with participation from Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate. Certain Energy is developing a manganese-based redox flow battery architecture designed for multi-hour to multi-day energy storage, targeting grid-scale applications where lithium-ion’s 4-hour duration ceiling is inadequate. The investment arrives as long-duration energy storage increasingly emerges as the enabling technology for high-penetration renewable grids that require seasonal and multi-day firming capacity.

science.overview_html: August 27’s science additions are directly relevant to this week’s dominant story. A new Communications Earth & Environment paper finds that more than 90% of Southeast Asia’s biomass-burning black carbon is char-BC — a combustion product that standard atmospheric models capture at only ~30% of observed concentrations — which, when corrected, more than doubles the estimated direct radiative forcing from 1.95 to 4.51 W/m². The result lands as Indonesia’s peatland fires have scaled to 285,000 ha. A companion Nature Reviews Earth & Environment comprehensive review of atmospheric black carbon in the climate system situates the char-BC gap within the broader picture: BC is both an underappreciated near-term warming agent and, through Arctic deposition, an accelerant of sea-ice albedo loss — the mechanism the Clean Arctic Alliance documented from this summer’s record boreal fire season. On the AI forecasting side, the week’s central result from Zhang et al. (Science Advances) — NWP outperforms AI for record-breaking extremes — and ECMWF’s AIFS-CRPS continue to draw operational discussion, with Tianmu-TC bearing live scrutiny as Typhoon Saudel makes landfall.

items.headline: SE Asia Biomass-Burning Black Carbon Is 90%+ Char-BC — Models Capture Only 30% of Observed BC; Direct Radiative Forcing Corrected from 1.95 to 4.51 W/m²
items.summary: This Communications Earth & Environment study characterizes black carbon (BC) from Southeast Asian biomass burning, finding that more than 90% of the region’s BB-related BC is char-black carbon — a high-temperature combustion product with distinct optical properties from soot-BC. Standard atmospheric models capture only approximately 30% of observed char-BC because they underrepresent the high-temperature combustion conditions typical of peatland and forest fires. Correcting for this omission nearly doubles the estimated direct aerosol radiative forcing from Southeast Asian fires: the corrected value is 4.51 W/m², compared to the previously reported 1.95 W/m². The finding is directly policy-relevant as Indonesia’s 2026 fire season has now burned 285,000 hectares under strong El Niño conditions, placing char-BC emissions from this season among the highest in the regional GFAS record.

items.headline: Atmospheric Black Carbon in the Climate System: Comprehensive Review Spans Emissions, Optical Properties, Transport, and Arctic Albedo Feedback
items.summary: This Nature Reviews Earth & Environment comprehensive review synthesizes the current state of knowledge on atmospheric black carbon (BC) as a climate forcing agent. The review covers BC emissions sources and inventories (industrial combustion, transport, biomass burning), atmospheric transport and removal processes, optical properties relevant to direct and indirect radiative forcing, and BC deposition on Arctic snow and sea ice — where albedo reduction accelerates melt in a feedback that is increasingly relevant given 2026’s record boreal and Southeast Asian fire season. The review discusses the substantial remaining uncertainty in BC’s net climate effect, spanning a range of +0.4 to +1.0 W/m² globally depending on co-emitted aerosol species and model treatment. The paper arrives as both Indonesia’s peatland fires and Yamal-Nenets’ record-high Arctic emissions make 2026 a natural-experiment year for constraining BC’s seasonal climate role.

items.title: Certain Energy Closes €11.6M Series A — British Business Bank, Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust Back Imperial College London Spinout’s Manganese Flow Battery for LDES
items.body_html: UK-based Certain Energy closed a €11.6 million Series A on August 26, 2026, led by the British Business Bank with participation from Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate. The company, spun out of Imperial College London, is developing a manganese-based redox flow battery designed for long-duration energy storage (LDES) applications — multi-hour to multi-day grid-scale firming where lithium-ion’s 4-hour ceiling is insufficient. Centrica’s participation signals strategic offtake interest and indicates that UK integrated energy companies are moving up the LDES value chain ahead of anticipated grid-balancing service markets under GB Capacity Market reform. The Temasek Trust Catalytic Capital for Climate commitment follows their mandate to de-risk climate-technology commercialization at the Series A stage across emerging and established markets.

items.title: MN8 Energy (NYSE: MNX) Acquires Greenbacker Capital Management for $375M — Deal Consolidates Renewable Energy Investment Services as Independent Power Sector Scales
items.body_html: MN8 Energy, the NYSE-listed renewable energy company (ticker: MNX), acquired Greenbacker Capital Management for approximately $375 million, as reported in Mondaq’s August 2026 Sustainable Energy Infrastructure roundup. Greenbacker Capital is a renewable energy-focused investment manager that has deployed capital across distributed and utility-scale solar, wind, and storage projects across North America. The transaction consolidates renewable energy investment-management services under a larger publicly traded operator at a time when independent power producers are scaling to compete with utility balance sheets for long-term PPA origination. The acquisition follows MN8’s NYSE listing and signals intent to build an integrated originate-own-operate-manage platform rather than a purely capital-light IPP model.
items.source_html: Mondaq Sustainable Energy Infrastructure / August 2026

items.title: Nth Cycle and Kensington Capital VI Complete Reverse Merger — Electrochemical Critical-Mineral Recycling Company Lists on NYSE Under “NTH” With ~$100M Development Capital
items.body_html: Nth Cycle and Kensington Capital VI completed a reverse merger reported in Mondaq’s August 2026 infrastructure roundup, bringing the electrochemical critical-mineral recycling company to NYSE listing under the ticker NTH with approximately $100 million in development capital. Nth Cycle’s core technology — the Oyster electro-extraction platform — recovers battery-grade cobalt, nickel, and manganese from black mass (spent EV battery cells and manufacturing scrap) using electrochemical separation rather than smelting, offering a lower-energy and higher-purity route to critical mineral supply. The NYSE listing provides Nth Cycle with the public capital access needed to scale commercial Oyster units alongside battery recyclers and cathode-active material producers, a market segment that is expected to grow rapidly as the first wave of mass-market EVs enters end-of-life.
items.source_html: Mondaq Sustainable Energy Infrastructure / August 2026
